# Landscape map

64 verified items across 8 layers · 0 relations · 15 open findings

## law-markup

- Akoma Ntoso / OASIS LegalDocML · **adopt** · active
  XML vocabulary for parliamentary, legislative and judicial documents (bills, acts, debates, judgments, amendments, collections); includes FRBR-based URI naming convention for point-in-time version addressing and a metadata model for lifecycle, temporal data, and references
  _why:_ AKN is the OASIS international standard for legislative document structure, providing FRBR-based URI naming (FRBRuri, FRBRthis, FRBRdate) for point-in-time law identification. It is the cross-jurisdictional alignment layer that USLM (US) and e-Gov (Japan) both overlap with, enabling uniform law citation across jurisdictions (cq-002). Its act/article/portion model also informs the source sublayer of clause decomposition (cq-001). Version 1.0 is the current OASIS Standard; v2.0/AKN 3.1 was in public comment at run time.
  https://www.oasis-open.org/standard/akn-v1-0/
- United States Legislative Markup (USLM) · **adopt** · active
  XML information model for US federal legislative documents including the US Code, bills, resolutions, statutes, and public laws; supports hierarchical document structure, positive-law codification, and stylistic variants (OLC, USC)
  _why:_ USLM 2.1.0 is the authoritative GPO XML schema for the US Code, bills, resolutions, and public laws. It directly provides versioned, addressable US federal primary law required by cq-002. The GitHub-hosted schema is the definitive source for positive-law codification structure and stylistic variants used by Congress.
  https://github.com/usgpo/uslm
- e-Gov 法令API / 法令標準XMLスキーマ (Japan Law XML Schema and API) · **adopt** · active
  XML schema (XSD) and HTTP API for Japanese primary law (statutes, cabinet orders, ministerial ordinances, notifications); provides full-text retrieval, article-level access, amendment history retrieval, and point-in-time versioning added in API v2
  _why:_ The Japan Digital Agency's e-Gov XML schema (XMLSchemaForJapaneseLaw_v3) and API v2 (released 2025-03-14) provide full-text retrieval, article-level access, amendment history, and point-in-time versioning for Japanese statutes, cabinet orders, and ministerial ordinances. This is the authoritative structured source for Japanese primary law (cq-002), directly relevant to the GK entity's governing jurisdiction.
  https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/docs/law-data-basic/419a603-xml-schema-for-japanese-law/
- Crown Legislation Markup Language (CLML) · **reference** · active · Crown copyright
  XML dialect for UK primary and secondary legislation published on legislation.gov.uk, covering acts, statutory instruments, explanatory notes, impact assessments, and point-in-time historical versions accessible via the legislation API
  _why:_ UK law is outside the primary jurisdiction scope (Japan, Delaware, US federal). However, CLML v2.6 is the most mature public implementation of historical-version access at article level with a documented API, and serves as a design reference for how to implement point-in-time versioning for our Japan and US law layers. Retained as a reference pattern, not as a data source.
  https://legislation.github.io/clml-schema/
- Formex (Formalized Exchange of Electronic Publications) v4 · **ignore** · active
  XML-based format for EU Official Journal publications including regulations, directives, decisions, and other EU legislative acts; defines logical markup for exchange between the Publications Office and contractors; most EUR-Lex documents with structured text are available in Formex
  _why:_ Formex is specific to EU Official Journal publications. EU law is outside the primary jurisdiction scope, and the potential Austrian entity was not included in the charter's primary scope. Formex provides no coverage for Japan, Delaware, or US federal law and is therefore not relevant to any charter need.
  https://op.europa.eu/en/web/eu-vocabularies/formex

## tooling

- Accord Project — Cicero · **adopt** · active · Apache-2.0
  Smart legal contract runtime: parses natural-language templates bound to Concerto data models, extracts structured clause data, and executes clause instances against JSON event payloads.
  _why:_ Cicero is the Linux Foundation runtime that parses natural-language contract templates bound to Concerto typed data models, extracts structured clause data, and executes clause logic against JSON event payloads. This directly realises clause-as-structured-object (cq-001), obligation execution (cq-003), template-driven drafting (cq-005), and lifecycle event processing (cq-011). Apache-2.0 licence and open governance make it suitable as a foundational tool layer.
  https://github.com/accordproject/cicero
- Catala · **adopt** · active · Apache-2.0
  Domain-specific language for compiling annotated legislative text to verified executable algorithms; embeds default logic as a first-class feature and produces lawyer-readable PDF proofs.
  _why:_ Catala compiles annotated legislative text into verified executable algorithms using prioritised default logic, with compiler correctness proved in F*. Its literate-programming approach keeps legal text and formal model in sync. This directly realises cq-003 (obligations as executable rules with conditions and breach consequences), cq-014 (formal semantics for statutory obligations), and cq-015 (scope definitions and priority rules provide algebraic composition of legal defaults). Apache-2.0, active, Inria-maintained.
  https://github.com/CatalaLang/catala
- Python-Redlines · **adopt** · active · MIT
  DOCX comparison tool producing native Word tracked-change redlines from two .docx input files; detects insertions, deletions, moves, and table/header/footer structural differences.
  _why:_ python-redlines generates native Word tracked-change redlines (insertions, deletions, moves, structural differences) from two .docx files. This directly implements the Word-redline negotiation workflow required by cq-006. Active, MIT-licensed, and the only verified open-source package providing this specific capability.
  https://github.com/JSv4/Python-Redlines
- python-docx-template (docxtpl) · **adopt** · active · LGPL-2.1
  Word document template engine using Jinja2 tags embedded in .docx files; populates templates with structured context data supporting conditional blocks, loops, rich text, inline images, and sub-document merging.
  _why:_ docxtpl's Jinja2-in-DOCX template engine projects the typed contract data model into the Word format counterparties expect, directly realising the 'PDF is only a projection' principle of cq-001 and template-driven drafting (cq-005). Lightweight, LGPL-licensed, widely used in legal document pipelines, and actively maintained.
  https://docxtpl.readthedocs.io/
- WeasyPrint · **adopt** · active · BSD
  HTML/CSS to PDF rendering engine using CSS Paged Media; converts structured HTML into paginated professional PDF documents including invoices, reports, and court forms.
  _why:_ WeasyPrint converts HTML/CSS using CSS Paged Media into paginated PDF. In the target architecture, the HTML layer is a structured rendering of the contract data model, making WeasyPrint the PDF-projection step required by cq-001. BSD-licensed and actively maintained.
  https://weasyprint.org/
- docassemble · **borrow** · active · MIT
  Guided interview and document assembly system: collects answers through a conditional web interview and assembles PDF, RTF, or DOCX output from templates.
  _why:_ docassemble's guided interview and conditional-branching document assembly pattern (interview → question blocks → template → DOCX/PDF) is the proven architecture for drafting from structured inputs (cq-005). However, docassemble is a UI layer without the typed semantic data model the charter requires; borrow the interview-driven assembly and conditional logic patterns rather than adopting it as a model layer.
  https://docassemble.org
- OpenFisca Core · **borrow** · active · AGPL-3.0
  Microsimulation engine for encoding tax and benefit rules as Python code; exposes a JSON web API and vectorial Python API for computing obligations, entitlements, and simulating policy reforms.
  _why:_ OpenFisca's Variable/Entity/Formula/Period model and JSON/Python API encode computable rules with parameter sensitivity analysis, applicable to cost-plus pricing and transfer-pricing computation (cq-008) and rule execution (cq-003). However, OpenFisca is primarily scoped to socio-fiscal microsimulation, not contract clause semantics; borrow its computation architecture and period-aware formula model rather than adopting it as a contract model layer.
  https://github.com/openfisca/openfisca-core
- LexNLP · **borrow** · dormant · AGPL-3.0
  NLP extraction library for unstructured legal text: segments sentences with legal-abbreviation awareness, extracts monetary amounts, dates, citations, courts, regulations, and classifies document and clause types.
  _why:_ LexNLP provides NLP extraction patterns for monetary amounts, dates, citations, courts, and regulations from unstructured legal text — relevant for drafting from meeting notes (cq-005) and clause review (cq-006). LexNLP is dormant since November 2022 (v2.3.0, no subsequent releases confirmed); borrow its extraction logic and legal-abbreviation-aware sentence parsing as patterns to adapt, not as a live dependency to adopt.
  https://github.com/LexPredict/lexpredict-lexnlp

## standard-forms

- Common Paper Standard Agreements · **adopt** · active · CC BY 4.0
  B2B commercial agreements including NDA, Cloud Service Agreement (SaaS), Professional Services Agreement, Software License Agreement, DPA, BAA, Terms of Service, SLA, and supporting documents, using a two-part Cover Page + hosted Standard Terms structure.
  _why:_ Common Paper provides NDA, Cloud Service Agreement, and Professional Services Agreement under CC BY 4.0 with a Cover Page + Standard Terms two-part structure. This parametric form design (variable Cover Page, stable Standard Terms incorporated by reference) is the pattern for drafting from a template (cq-005) and reviewing against a known position (cq-006). The Professional Services Agreement is directly applicable to services between the GK and C-corp (cq-008 context).
  https://commonpaper.com/standards/
- Y Combinator SAFE (Simple Agreement for Future Equity) · **adopt** · active · Free to download and use
  Startup financing instrument: a short contract for investors to fund a startup now in exchange for shares later, with variants for valuation cap, discount rate, and MFN terms; plus a Pro Rata Side Letter.
  _why:_ The YC Post-Money SAFE is the industry-standard instrument for pre-seed startup financing, with variants for valuation cap, discount rate, and MFN. It directly provides the canonical form for cq-010 (SAFEs and founder stock). Freely available from Y Combinator and widely accepted by investors and counsel in the US and internationally.
  https://www.ycombinator.com/documents
- NVCA Model Legal Documents · **adopt** · active · Free (no CC licence stated)
  Industry-standard venture capital financing documents for US preferred stock rounds: certificate of incorporation, stock purchase agreement, investors' rights agreement, voting agreement, right of first refusal and co-sale agreement, management rights letter, indemnification agreement, PIPE financing documents, and university biotech/climate tech licensing templates.
  _why:_ NVCA Model Legal Documents (October 2025) are the industry standard for venture capital financing and Delaware corporate governance. They cover Certificate of Incorporation, Stock Purchase Agreement, Investors' Rights Agreement, Voting Agreement, Board Consent, and Stockholder Consent — directly serving cq-009 (corporate governance instruments for the C-corp) and cq-010 (startup financing preferred-stock mechanics).
  https://nvca.org/model-legal-documents/
- IPA 情報システム・モデル取引・契約書 (Information System Model Transaction Contract) · **adopt** · active
  Model contracts and transaction frameworks for IT system development between user companies and IT vendors in Japan, covering commissioned development, maintenance, operations, SaaS/package software, and agile development methodologies.
  _why:_ IPA 情報システム・モデル取引・契約書 (Second Edition + Agile Edition) are the Japanese government-endorsed model contracts for IT system development. They directly govern services between a Japanese technology provider (the GK) and a user company under commissioned-development, maintenance/operations, and agile frameworks (cq-008, cq-009). The most authoritative Japanese-language IT contract templates available and the baseline for services agreement drafting in Japan (cq-005).
  https://www.ipa.go.jp/digital/model/index.html
- Bonterms Standard Agreements · **borrow** · active · CC BY 4.0 (Standard Agreements); CC0 1.0 (Playbook Items)
  Neutral enterprise commercial agreements including Mutual NDA, Cloud Terms (SaaS), Professional Services Agreement, Data Protection Addendum, Business Associate Agreement, Software License Terms, and AI Standard Clauses; validated by a committee of 120+ lawyers.
  _why:_ Bonterms targets the same B2B agreement types as Common Paper (NDA, Cloud Terms, PSA) and is a direct substitute. Its additional AI Standard Clauses and UK/EU jurisdiction variants add coverage beyond Common Paper's scope. Borrow the AI clauses and cross-jurisdictional term variants as supplementary content rather than adopting a competing primary form standard.
  https://bonterms.com/
- Cooley GO Legal Document Generators · **reference** · active · Free to use (proprietary; no CC licence stated)
  Generator-based startup legal document suite covering Delaware/Nevada incorporation, SAFE, NVCA financing, Series Seed equity and notes, convertible notes, NDA, employee CIIA, advisor agreements, and cap tables.
  _why:_ Cooley GO generates NVCA and YC SAFE documents (both already adopted) as parametric outputs, demonstrating how Cover Page + Standard Terms can be realised as a generator. Useful as a reference for parametric form generation design (cq-005), but it is a proprietary tool whose documents are derived from NVCA/SAFE. No distinct content or open schema to adopt beyond what is already covered.
  https://www.cooleygo.com/documents/

## provenance

- PROV-O: The PROV Ontology · **adopt** · active · W3C Document License
  Provenance of resources: activities, entities, and agents involved in producing, influencing, or delivering a piece of data or thing; supports expressing lineage, derivation chains, and attribution for any resource including legal documents and derived records.
  _why:_ PROV-O (W3C Recommendation 2013) provides the OWL ontology for expressing provenance — entities, activities, agents, derivation chains (prov:wasDerivedFrom), and attribution (prov:wasAttributedTo). It is the standard model for expressing lineage of clauses back to statutory sources (cq-001: source sublayer), and for attributing and tracing primary law references to their origins (cq-002). Its prov:Bundle supports named provenance graphs for each instrument version.
  https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/
- Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) / ISO 17442 · **adopt** · active · public good, available free of charge to all users
  Persistent unique identity of legal entities (companies, partnerships, trusts, governmental bodies) participating in financial and legal transactions; Level 1 Data identifies who the entity is, Level 2 Data captures ownership and relationship structure.
  _why:_ GLEIF LEI (ISO 17442:2020) provides globally unique, persistent 20-character codes for legal entities with Level 1 (entity identity) and Level 2 (ownership/relationship structure) data freely accessible via the Global LEI Index. Using LEI codes as canonical party identifiers ensures unambiguous identification of the GK, the C-corp, and counterparties in obligations (cq-003: who bears which obligation) and authority records (cq-004: which entity is being bound).
  https://www.gleif.org/en/organizational-identity/introducing-the-legal-entity-identifier-lei/iso-17442-the-lei-code-structure
- URN:LEX — URN Namespace for Sources of Law (RFC 9676) · **adopt** · active · IETF Trust copyright
  Persistent, location-independent, language-neutral unique identifiers for sources of law (legislation, case law, administrative acts, regulations) across any jurisdiction; applies the FRBR Work/Expression/Manifestation/Item hierarchy to legal documents to support point-in-time versioning and language variants.
  _why:_ URN:LEX (RFC 9676) provides persistent, location-independent, jurisdiction-neutral identifiers for sources of law using the FRBR Work/Expression/Manifestation/Item hierarchy with jurisdiction/work/expression partition-ids. As the IETF-published specification for law URNs across any jurisdiction, it is the URI scheme for citing Japanese, US federal, and Delaware primary law with version precision — directly serving the 'versioned, addressable primary law with lineage' requirement of cq-002.
  https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9676
- W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0 · **adopt** · active · W3C Software and Document Notice and License
  Tamper-evident, cryptographically verifiable credentials representing claims about a subject; provides the data model for digitally signed assertions about identity, authorizations, qualifications, and provenance that can be issued, held, and verified by distinct parties — applicable to signing authority, party credentials, and document authenticity.
  _why:_ W3C VC Data Model v2.0 (Recommendation 2025-05-15) provides tamper-evident, cryptographically verifiable credentials for claims about subjects. For cq-004, a VC can attest that a named individual holds authority to bind a specific entity (identified by LEI) for a specified scope. The credentialSubject, issuer, validFrom, validUntil, and termsOfUse fields provide the structural slots for an authority grant credential, subject to additional schema work to model scope and monetary limits.
  https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/
- Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.1 · **borrow** · draft
  Globally unique, persistent, cryptographically verifiable identifiers for subjects (persons, organizations, documents) that do not require a central registration authority; each DID resolves to a DID Document containing cryptographic keys and service endpoints enabling verifiable interactions.
  _why:_ W3C DID v1.1 (Candidate Recommendation, 2026-03-05) provides cryptographically verifiable, decentralized identifiers for parties and documents — the identity layer that W3C VC depends on for issuer and subject identification (cq-004). Borrow the DID resolution pattern for identity infrastructure. DID v1.1 has not reached full Recommendation status at run time; DID method selection for our specific use case requires further evaluation before full adoption.
  https://www.w3.org/TR/did-1.1/
- DCMI Metadata Terms (provenance vocabulary) · **borrow** · active
  General-purpose metadata vocabulary for describing resources; includes provenance-specific terms recording custody history, ownership changes, and versioning relationships (isVersionOf, replaces, hasVersion) together with attribution terms (creator, contributor) — provides lightweight provenance properties compatible with PROV-O.
  _why:_ DCMI Terms provides lightweight provenance properties (dct:provenance, dct:isVersionOf, dct:replaces, dct:creator, dct:created) that are a practical complement to PROV-O for standard document metadata. Borrow the dc:terms vocabulary for bibliographic metadata on instruments (creator, date, version lineage) while PROV-O handles structural derivation graphs. The two vocabularies are explicitly aligned in the scan relator output.
  https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/
- European Legislation Identifier (ELI) · **reference** · active
  Identification, metadata description, and point-in-time versioning of European and national legislation; assigns URIs to legislative acts and provides an OWL ontology following FRBR principles to express relationships between versions, expressions, and formats of laws, plus cross-border legislative references.
  _why:_ ELI provides HTTP URIs and OWL metadata (eli:LegalResource, eli:LegalExpression) for EU and national legislation using FRBR-based point-in-time versioning. EU law is outside primary scope, but ELI's ontology is the closest formal model to what is needed for law citation metadata and directly informed the URN:LEX design. Reference for provenance design of Japan and US federal law sources.
  https://op.europa.eu/en/web/eu-vocabularies/eli
- Digital Object Identifier System (DOI) / ISO 26324 · **reference** · active
  Persistent, semantically interoperable identifiers for intellectual content objects (documents, data sets, standards) that resolve to current metadata and location regardless of where the object moves; relevant for giving legal instruments and their versions persistent, citable, resolvable identities.
  _why:_ DOI / ISO 26324:2025 provides persistent, citable, resolvable identifiers for intellectual content objects. URN:LEX and AKN FRBR URIs are more appropriate for primary law, and PROV-O handles document lineage. DOI is the appropriate citation identifier for published academic papers and standards cited in our model (e.g., Composing Contracts, Catala papers), but not the primary identifier system for instruments or legislation.
  https://www.doi.org/the-identifier/resources/factsheets/doi-system-and-the-handle-system

## clause-corpora

- CUAD: Contract Understanding Atticus Dataset · **adopt** · active · CC BY 4.0
  510 commercial contracts expert-annotated with 13,000+ labels across 41 clause categories to train and evaluate contract review question-answering models.
  _why:_ CUAD's 41 clause categories — including Change of Control, IP Ownership Assignment, Governing Law, Most Favored Nation, and Termination For Convenience — provide an expert-validated taxonomy for the clause types we need to identify in review (cq-006), track (cq-011), and query across a portfolio (cq-012). The IP Ownership Assignment category directly supports cq-007. The 510-contract, 13,000+ annotation corpus is the primary training data source for clause extraction models. CC BY 4.0.
  https://www.atticusprojectai.org/cuad
- ACORD: Atticus Clause Retrieval Dataset · **adopt** · active · CC BY 4.0
  Clause retrieval benchmark: 114 expert queries with 126,000+ rated clause pairs graded 1-5 stars for training retrieval models that support contract drafting from precedent.
  _why:_ ACORD provides 114 expert-annotated retrieval queries with 126,000+ ranked clause pairs (1–5 stars) for clause types including Limitation of Liability, Indemnification, Change of Control, and MFN. This is the only verified retrieval benchmark fully annotated by experts for contract drafting: it directly supports drafting from precedent (cq-005: find the closest matching precedent clause) and benchmarking our review models against market-standard clause quality (cq-006). CC BY 4.0.
  https://www.atticusprojectai.org/acord
- LEDGAR: Large-Scale Multi-label Corpus for Legal Provisions · **borrow** · active · CC BY 4.0
  Multi-label text classification of nearly 100,000 contract provisions from 60,000+ SEC EDGAR contracts across 12,000+ provision topic labels.
  _why:_ LEDGAR's 100,000 provisions across 12,000+ topic labels provides a broader provision-classification taxonomy than CUAD's 41 categories. Its multi-label approach informs how a single clause can serve multiple legal purposes. Borrow as supplementary training data and evidence that provision classification generalises beyond CUAD — CUAD is adopted as the primary taxonomy.
  https://aclanthology.org/2020.lrec-1.155/
- MAUD: Merger Agreement Understanding Dataset · **borrow** · active · CC BY 4.0
  47,000+ expert annotations on 152 public merger agreements covering deal point classification for M&A contract review.
  _why:_ MAUD provides 47,000+ expert annotations on 152 merger agreements covering M&A deal points (change-of-control, MAC, representations and warranties, termination rights). Directly relevant for change-of-control clause queries in cq-012 and for reviewing acquisition documents in cq-006. Borrow as training data and as the M&A segment of the clause taxonomy.
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.00876
- ContractNLI: Dataset for Document-level NLI on Contracts · **borrow** · active · CC BY 4.0
  607 NDAs annotated with entailment/contradiction/not-mentioned labels for 17 fixed hypotheses, supporting automated NDA clause review and evidence span identification.
  _why:_ ContractNLI provides document-level NLI labels (entailment/contradiction/not-mentioned) for 17 fixed hypotheses on 607 NDAs, supporting automated review of NDA clauses against a known position (cq-006). Borrow as the evaluation framework and training data for the NDA clause review component, where the hypothesis-testing model maps directly to our review-against-positions need.
  https://stanfordnlp.github.io/contract-nli/
- Pile of Law · **borrow** · active · CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
  256GB+ open pretraining corpus including US contracts (Atticus Project, SEC EDGAR, CFPB credit card agreements, Terms of Service), court opinions, legislation, and regulatory filings.
  _why:_ Pile of Law provides 256GB+ of legal pretraining data (US contracts, court opinions, legislation, regulations) for building or fine-tuning legal language models used in drafting (cq-005) and extraction. Borrow as a pretraining corpus for LLM components in the drafting pipeline. Note: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence restricts commercial use; this constraint must be tracked in any production deployment.
  https://huggingface.co/datasets/pile-of-law/pile-of-law
- Material Contracts Corpus (MCC) · **borrow** · active · CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
  1M+ SEC EDGAR Exhibit-10 material contracts (2000-2023) with ML-generated contract type labels, party identification, and metadata linking to original filings.
  _why:_ MCC provides 1M+ SEC Exhibit-10 material contracts (2000–2023) with ML-generated contract type labels, party identification, and EDGAR metadata. The scale and labelling make it the best open corpus for training contract-type classifiers and clause-extraction models for drafting from precedent (cq-005) and portfolio classification (cq-012). CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 restricts commercial use.
  https://mcc.law.stanford.edu
- MultiLegalPile: 689GB Multilingual Legal Corpus · **borrow** · active
  689GB multilingual pretraining corpus covering 24 languages and 17 jurisdictions; no clause-level annotations but relevant for multilingual legal model pretraining spanning European and other languages.
  _why:_ MultiLegalPile covers 24 languages across 17 jurisdictions as a 689GB pretraining corpus, and is the largest available multilingual legal pretraining corpus. Although it lacks clause-level annotations, it is the primary resource for training Japanese-language legal NLP components required by cq-013. No verified Japanese-specific annotated corpus was found in any layer; MultiLegalPile is the best available foundation for Japanese language coverage. Licence not confirmed in scan; usage terms must be verified.
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02069
- SALI LMSS: Legal Matter Standard Specification · **reference** · active · CC BY ND
  OWL ontology providing 18,000+ tagged concepts for classifying legal work by area of law, service type, industry, and player role; each tag carries a stable IRI enabling interoperability across legal management systems.
  _why:_ SALI LMSS provides 18,000+ tagged concepts for classifying legal work by area of law, service type, industry, and player role, with stable IRIs for interoperability. As a matter-classification taxonomy rather than a contract data model, it is a reference for tagging portfolio instruments by area of law and enabling cross-system interoperability in cq-012 (portfolio querying for diligence). Not a clause-level or obligation-level model to adopt.
  https://sali.org/explore-the-standard/
- LexGLUE: Benchmark for Legal Language Understanding in English · **reference** · active · CC BY 4.0
  Multi-task legal NLP benchmark integrating seven datasets including LEDGAR (provision classification), UNFAIR-ToS (clause fairness), ECtHR decisions, SCOTUS opinions, EUR-LEX regulation classification, and ContractNLI.
  _why:_ LexGLUE is a multi-task legal NLP benchmark integrating LEDGAR, ContractNLI, and other datasets for standardised evaluation of legal language understanding. It is the reference for evaluating our clause extraction and review models against published baselines (cq-006). Informative for model evaluation design but not a data layer or tool to directly adopt.
  https://aclanthology.org/2022.acl-long.297/

## ip-licensing

- W3C ODRL Information Model 2.2 · **adopt** · active · W3C permissive document license
  Policy expression language for representing usage rights, permissions, prohibitions, and obligations over digital assets. Applicable to IP licensing: Permission (right to act over an Asset), Prohibition, Duty (obligation), Constraint (territory/purpose/time), Asset (licensed work), Party (licensor/licensee), and action vocabulary including distribute, reproduce, derive, and transfer.
  _why:_ ODRL 2.2 (W3C Recommendation) provides Policy/Permission/Prohibition/Duty/Asset/Party/Constraint as the formal model for expressing usage rights and obligations over digital assets. It directly models IP licences (cq-007: who has what rights over which assets under what territorial/purpose constraints), obligations arising from rights grants (cq-003), and compositional policy structures (cq-015: policies can be combined, overridden, and checked). The Spatial constraint maps to the Japan vs RoW territorial split in the IP licensing layer.
  https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/
- SPDX — Software Package Data Exchange · **adopt** · active · CC-BY-3.0
  Standard for communicating software package licence and copyright information: associates every file, package, or snippet with a machine-readable licence identifier (SPDX-License-Identifier), enabling automated compliance and IP chain-of-title tracing for software artefacts.
  _why:_ SPDX 3.0.1 (Linux Foundation) is the standard for software package licence and copyright communication via SPDX-License-Identifier and LicenseExpression. Given that the GK owns software IP licensed to the C-corp, SPDX provides the mechanism for communicating licence terms and IP chain-of-title for every software component — directly serving cq-007 (IP rights, assignments, and software asset lineage).
  https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v2.3/
- DALICC — Data Licenses Clearance Center · **borrow**
  ODRL-based vocabulary and framework for modelling data-asset licences as machine-readable policies (permissions, duties, prohibitions) with a dependency graph encoding 'included-in', 'implies', and 'contradicts' relationships between actions, enabling automated licence compatibility checking and rights clearance.
  _why:_ DALICC extends ODRL with a licence-compatibility dependency graph (implies/contradicts/included-in relations between licence actions), enabling automated licence compatibility checking. This is directly applicable to checking whether IP licences can be combined or conflict (cq-015: algebraic checking of obligations), particularly across the Japan vs RoW territorial split in our IP rights layer (cq-007). Borrow the dependency-graph approach into our ODRL-based IP model.
  https://dalicc.github.io/
- Creative Commons Rights Expression Language (ccREL) · **reference** · active · CC BY 4.0
  RDF vocabulary for describing copyright licences and attaching them machine-readably to works: permissions (reproduce, distribute, derivative works), requirements (attribution, share-alike, source code), prohibitions (commercial use), jurisdiction, and link to legal code.
  _why:_ ccREL is the domain-specific precursor to ODRL, mapping cc:permits/cc:requires/cc:prohibits to ODRL's Permission/Duty/Prohibition. Since ODRL is adopted as the IP rights model, ccREL is retained as a reference for understanding how CC-licensed content expresses rights in RDF. It adds no distinct capability beyond what ODRL covers for our IP model.
  https://www.w3.org/submissions/2008/SUBM-ccREL-20080501/
- WIPO Standard ST.96 — IP XML Schemas v7.0 · **reference** · active
  XML schemas for inter-office exchange of IP information across five categories: patents, trademarks, industrial designs, geographical indications, and copyright (orphan works), including common data components shared across IP types. Used for inter-office communication and office-system implementation by national IP offices.
  _why:_ WIPO ST.96 v7.0 XML schemas cover IP data exchange between national IP offices across patents, trademarks, and designs. Relevant for reading and exchanging patent/trademark bibliographic data when the GK's IP portfolio is referenced in licence agreements (cq-007).
